subject: DPA clarifications - Nimbus Payments
messages:
From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
To: Sam Lee <sam.lee@nimbus-payments.com>
Cc: Lauren Bishop <lauren.bishop@redwood.com>, Vivek Kulkarni <vivek.kulkarni@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 09 Nov 2026 15:12:00 -0800
Subject: DPA clarifications - Nimbus Payments

Sam / Aisha —

Thanks again for the call earlier — great to learn more about Nimbus' onboarding flow and the sensitive PII elements you ingest (payments metadata, cardholder name, partial PAN, and customer support transcripts). Per our discussion, I wanted to capture the follow-ups we promised and proposed next steps so we can keep procurement moving.

Recap / asks from Nimbus:
- Confirmed PII types: cardholder name, last4, email, support transcripts (sensitive).
- Data residency requirement: you asked about EU residency for EU customers (eu-west-1).
- Retention / logging: default request retention vs. audit logs, retention windows, and deletion confirmation on contract termination.
- Controller/Processor roles: you asked for explicit language on controller vs processor responsibilities in the DPA.
- Subprocessors & breach notice: requested list of subprocessors and SLA for breach notification (you asked for 72-hour notice).
- SOC 2 report availability behind NDA.

What I will do (next steps on Redwood side):
1) Share current DPA and subprocessor list (attached: DPA_v1.pdf).
2) Confirm default retention and options for enterprise accounts.
3) Ask Legal to draft proposed language addressing controller/processor classification and breach timing.
4) Schedule a short follow-up call with you and our legal lead if you want to walk through redlines (I can get Vivek on the thread).

Proposed timeline: I’ll get an updated DPA + subprocessor list to you by end of day tomorrow (Tue 11/10). If that works, let me know when you’d like to review.

Thanks — looking forward to keeping momentum.

Best,
Marissa Cole
Account Executive | Redwood Inference
marissa.cole@redwood.com | +1 415-555-0198

Attachments: DPA_v1.pdf (PDF, 42KB)

From: Sam Lee <sam.lee@nimbus-payments.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 10 Nov 2026 09:03:00 -05:00
Subject: Re: DPA clarifications - Nimbus Payments

Thanks Marissa — appreciate the recap and quick turnaround. A few clarifying questions from our legal and security teams after reviewing the attached DPA:

1) Controller/Processor: We need explicit confirmation that Nimbus is the Controller and Redwood is the Processor for any PII we send to the service. We also want a short clause describing handling of telemetry/metrics (we consider aggregated metrics non-PII).
2) Subprocessors: Please send the full current list of subprocessors and confirm the notification process when you add a new subprocessor.
3) Breach notice: Our compliance team asked for a 72-hour notification window for confirmed breaches impacting PII. Will Redwood commit to 72 hours for initial notification?
4) Data residency: For EU customers, can you guarantee storage & compute strictly in eu-west-1 (including KV cache and backups)? If not guaranteed, what are the controls and contract language we can use?
5) Retention & deletion: We need configurable retention windows for transcripts / logs and a deletion confirmation within 30 days of contract termination.
6) SOC 2: Please advise how we can receive your SOC 2 report (NDA/portal).

Can you loop in your legal contact so we can get proposed contract language and the subprocessor list? Happy to set a 30-minute call after you share the updated DPA.

Thanks,
Sam
Sam Lee | Head of Security & Compliance
Nimbus Payments
sam.lee@nimbus-payments.com | +1 646-555-2100

Subject: Fwd: DPA clarifications - Nimbus Payments / internal

Vivek / Lauren — forwarding Nimbus' follow-up questions (attached: sam_questions.pdf). They want explicit controller/processor language, subprocessor list, 72-hour breach notification, data residency guarantees for eu-west-1, and deletion confirmation within 30 days.

Notes / asks for Legal:
- What is our standard position on controller/processor? I believe we are processor for customer PII; we collect telemetry/metrics as a separate category (aggregate). Can we confirm wording?
- Breach notification: they request 72 hours — is that acceptable or do we need 48/72 compromise language?
- Data residency: can we offer pinned-eu deploy option for enterprise customers (private deployment or dedicated capacity)? If so, what language should we use for the hosted API?
- Retention: default request log retention is 90 days; enterprise configurable. Need proposed language to guarantee deletion within 30 days after termination.

Goal: produce a DPA redline (or short addendum) addressing each point by EOD (preferably). I told Sam we'd aim to share an updated DPA + subprocessor list by end of day today.

Thanks —
Marissa

Attachments: sam_questions.pdf (PDF, 8KB)

From: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek.kulkarni@redwood.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>, Lauren Bishop <lauren.bishop@redwood.com>
Cc: Sam Lee <sam.lee@nimbus-payments.com>
Date: Tue, 10 Nov 2026 13:45:00 -08:00
Subject: Re: Fwd: DPA clarifications - Nimbus Payments / internal

Hi team — quick draft responses and recommended DPA language to address Nimbus' asks. High level answers below; I'll prepare a redline and subprocessor export for them to review.

1) Controller / Processor:
- Position: Nimbus remains Controller; Redwood acts as Processor for customer PII processed through our inference platform. We will add a short clause: "Customer is Controller and Redwood is Processor with respect to Personal Data processed on behalf of Customer; Redwood may process aggregated/anonymous telemetry for internal product improvement purposes, which is not treated as Personal Data."

2) Subprocessors:
- We'll attach current subprocessor list (cloud infra providers, observability vendor, SSO provider). Standard process: notify customers 30 days prior to onboarding a new subprocessor and provide reasonable objection rights for contractually material changes.

3) Breach notice:
- We typically commit to "prompt" notification and will provide initial notification within 72 hours for confirmed incidents that materially impact Personal Data. We can commit to 72 hours for initial notification and follow-up as more info becomes available.

4) Data residency:
- Hosted API: we cannot guarantee compute residency for all hosted accounts by default, but for enterprise customers we offer Dedicated or Private deployments that can be pinned to eu-west-1. For Nimbus: if they require strict residency, propose Dedicated (reserved capacity) in eu-west-1; include a DPA Addendum that states data will be stored and processed in the designated region absent lawful requirements to the contrary.

5) Retention & deletion:
- Default request/trace retention: 90 days. Enterprise option: configurable retention as short as 30 days. Commit to purge or delete Customer Data within 30 days of contract termination for enterprise accounts with documented deletion playbook; provide deletion certificate upon request.

6) SOC 2:
- SOC 2 Type II report available under NDA. We'll provide a secure link post-NDA or via customer portal.

Next steps: I'll prepare a DPA redline that: (a) inserts the controller/processor clause above; (b) includes subprocessor notification language; (c) explicitly states 72-hour initial breach notification; (d) outlines residency options and references Dedicated/Private as residency guarantee; (e) adds deletion timing and certificate language. I will attach the DPA redline and current subprocessor list in my next email.

If you want, Marissa, you can send the above summary to Sam now and say legal will follow with the redline + list in ~2 hours.

Vivek
General Counsel | Redwood Inference
vivek.kulkarni@redwood.com

From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
To: Sam Lee <sam.lee@nimbus-payments.com>, Aisha Nair <aisha.nair@nimbus-payments.com>
Cc: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek.kulkarni@redwood.com>, Lauren Bishop <lauren.bishop@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 11 Nov 2026 11:04:00 -08:00
Subject: Re: DPA clarifications - Nimbus Payments

Sam / Aisha — quick update and attached items per our legal team's draft.

Summary of responses (legal-provided):
- Controller/Processor: Confirmed — Nimbus is Controller; Redwood is Processor. Draft clause included in attached DPA redline.
- Subprocessors: Attached current subprocessor_list.csv. Redwood will notify customers 30 days before onboarding a new subprocessor and provide a description of its role.
- Breach notice: Redwood will provide initial notification for confirmed incidents materially affecting Personal Data within 72 hours, with continuing updates.
- Data residency: For a strict EU residency guarantee we recommend Redwood Dedicated in eu-west-1. We will include a residency addendum in the DPA for Dedicated customers. Hosted accounts do not receive a hard residency guarantee by default.
- Retention & deletion: Default retention is 90 days; enterprise option allows configurable retention as low as 30 days. For Dedicated/Private customers we can guarantee deletion within 30 days of termination and provide a deletion certificate.
- SOC 2: Available via NDA — let me know if you'd like the SOC 2 link and I'll route the access request.

Attachments: DPA_Redwood_Draft_v2.pdf (redline), subprocessor_list.csv

Next steps: Would you like to schedule a 30-minute call with Vivek + me to walk through any redlines, or would you prefer to iterate asynchronously via DocuSign/HubSpot?

Best,
Marissa
Account Executive | Redwood Inference
